artworks.title: Circe Turning King Picus into a Woodpecker
artworks.description: Lubieniecki paints Ovid's Latian king mid-metamorphosis: Circe's wand raised, feathers already sprouting on Picus's arms. National Museum in Warsaw.

artworks.title: Picus and Circe
artworks.description: Giordano's Neapolitan oil stages Circe's rejected courtship of Picus — the woodpecker-king before the spell that will punish his fidelity to Canens.

artworks.title: Circe Changing Picus into a Bird
artworks.description: A Metamorphoses plate from the Metropolitan Museum series: Circe's companions drive Picus as wings break from his body. Print culture for the Latin woodpecker-king.

artworks.title: Circe Changes Picus into a Woodpecker
artworks.description: A Rijksmuseum Metamorphoses print shows Circe's circle watching Picus take flight — the king of Latium becoming the bird that still bears his name in Roman augury.

popCulture.title: Picus
popCulture.description: Saturn's son, king of Latium, woodpecker after Circe — the bird that still guides Roman augury in his name.
